<a id="done-when"></a>

## Done when

The seat runs on the new model or effort, resumed with its context, with the cache-proxy environment its model needs, and pij lists it registered on the new process.

<a id="known-limits"></a>

## Known limits

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| l-1 | The relaunch does not refresh pij's record of the seat: `pij-rs list` keeps the model and effort pij launched it with (`pij sessions --history --seat &lt;seat&gt;` too), and a later `pij-rs revive` puts the seat back on them. `pij-rs revive &lt;seat&gt; --model &lt;id&gt;` revives on a new model; `pij revive --effort` is an open item in the operator's queue. Seen live on 2026-11-26: after a relaunch on xhigh the record still read medium. |
| l-2 | pij records the relaunched seat's route as none (`cache_proxy: null` in `pij-rs list`), not proxied: the new process doesn't descend from the launch the daemon stamped (F213). A Claude seat's traffic still goes through the cache proxy, because the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment came with it (check the pane's process with `ps -Eww -p &lt;pid&gt;`). |
| l-3 | The relaunched process runs without `pij-rs __spawn-child`, so if it exits there is no exit-status file or launch log for a post-mortem. |
| l-4 | The seat's flags come from `ps`, which joins arguments with spaces, so a flag value that holds a space comes back as two words. |
| l-5 | A PIJ_* or COPILOT_* variable whose name holds KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, CREDENTIAL or AUTH is not carried (req-13). The script names each one it leaves out; a seat that needs one must get it again another way. |
| l-6 | A seat that ran plain stays plain on a new Claude model: only a pij spawn or revive runs the cache-proxy gate, and the script says so. To put it behind the proxy, revive it on that model (`pij-rs revive &lt;seat&gt; --model &lt;id&gt;`) once its process has ended. |
| l-7 | The script checks a model id's shape, not that Copilot serves it. A model Copilot refuses ends the new process, and the pane with it; rerun the procedure with the old model (`pij sessions --history --seat &lt;seat&gt;` names it) or revive the seat. |

<a id="mistakes"></a>

## Mistakes

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| m-1 | Dropping the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment of a seat that stays on Claude: the seat silently leaves the cache proxy and its next wake after five minutes idle rebuilds its whole context. |
| m-2 | Carrying PIJ_SPAWN_ID: it ties the new process to a spawn that has finished. |
| m-3 | Leaving out --resume=&lt;session&gt;: the seat starts a new conversation and loses its context. |
| m-4 | Using `/settings effortLevel` (changes the default for every new session), `/restart` (keeps the old flag) or `/model` in the session (the process keeps the launch's COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment, which names the old model and, for a model that is not Claude, sends it to the Anthropic-only proxy). |
| m-5 | Putting the seat's environment on the respawn command line: every value is then readable through `ps` by any local user and logged by the endpoint scanner. The script passes values through a 0600 file the pane reads and deletes. |
| m-6 | Keeping COPILOT_PROVIDER_* when moving a seat to a GPT (or any other non-Claude) model: the proxy serves Claude models only, so the model must run plain Copilot. |
| m-7 | Treating COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS as a secret because its name holds TOKEN: it is the model's prompt limit, and dropping it leaves a proxied seat without its 1M window. The script carries it by exact name. |
| m-8 | Reading the seat's flags and environment from pij's recorded pid. After a Copilot `/restart` that process is the loader's child: its argv has no --model or --effort, and its environment holds the loader's own variables. The script reads the pane's own process (`tmux display-message -p -t &lt;pane&gt; '#{pane_pid}'`), which is the launch. |
